It really depends on the kid so I hesitate to give any advice. You know your kid best.It seems like either an all or nothing approach here. Either take away all the toys and games and trips and all screen time completely for awhile. Being bored won't hurt the kid and will be forced to get creative.OR, all, let him have all of it and all the screen time he wants.In our case my kids were never restricted on screen time and honestly, they got bored with TV. They would stop watching to go play, or they would go act out what they saw on TV.They played with all their toys and also with rocks, sticks, dirt, and whatever. We only did short day trips. Parks and zoo etc. And mostly it was just the park or shopping really. And they always had a blast and entertained themselves.My mom once suggested I have fewer toys but my kids literally played with everything so I kept it all.It is hard to know what will work. But maybe, maybe just letting him have at the TV will work? I dunno.My son was (against my wishes) allowed video games at age 5. I wanted to wait until 12 for video games but my husband is a gamer so that well, he just ignored my wishes. But my son got really into them at age 5, however despite that he now at 10 does a great job of not playing too much. He will say, "I've been sitting too long, I need to go play outside." All I have done is talk about the importance of movement and exercise and I do have him in acrobatic classes the last 4 years. So he doesn't want to get weak he says. He won't sit too much.So for us a combo of freedom to choose as well as regular exercise and kind of just nudging gently toward activity has worked well for balance. Hope there was something in this rambling comment that helps.In the end just remember, kids get bored, it certainly won't hurt them.My response to "I'm bored" is usually, oh ok go clean your room. Or, "it's good for you." They know I won't go out of my way to cure their boredom. I think because of that they just had to figure out how to fix it themselves.   
We have activities we do together, but they need to know how to entertain themselves.

NSVs: Just realized I have been logging my food daily for over a week. I started toward the very end of March, forget which day. And the time has truly flown by because I am not on this super crazy strict eating plan. I am enjoying this and feeling just fine about it.   
Another win,  I am finding it amazing how often I have the urge to eat for reasons other than hunger. I knew I did this, but I am much more aware of it lately as I am working to stay in my calorie range. And I realize well, I don't really want it because I really am not hungry now. I really rather eat something better and nicer than a bag of chips or cheap packaged cookies later when my body is really asking for food. And it always taste better and is more enjoyable to eat when I am really hungry. On top of that, I don't feel like a fat slob after I eat because I am not stuffed with too much food.   
And amazingly I find myself turning down even fast food or other things I used to eat in large amounts because I don't want to waste the calories on that greasy food that doesn't make me feel very well. I rather eat like a small sweet treat or a larger serving of rice or something. So I'm really making each bite count, either I really just enjoy the food so much or it is very nutritious. But no more wasting calories on tons of crap food. but I'm not forbidding myself to do so either, and that helps.   
All of these may sound like simple things but they are huge wins for me from my old all or nothing mentality of eating. I used to either eat perfect and have cravings constantly, counting the days and time inching away so slowly. Or I gave up and binged all the time.

Thank you! I also realized that in the past when I had an off day I was likely eating over the number of calories needed to just maintain my current weight. But to be able to take control and just keep under that number if I want to have a "cheat" day blows my mind. It is like for the first time ever I am just certain, this is gonna work. Sorry this is really super ranty and long... I had to let this out somewhere.I think I have said this before here but it is really bothering me today. I'm rather angry at all the fat logic. Even though most of the fat logic I have been exposed to my entire life has been rather on the light side, not quite so crazy as the things posted here, it has had a huge effect on me and my health. Nobody seems to want to talk about the negative health effects of being fat. Nobody really spells it out or is honest about it. Maybe they don't know either? Maybe they don't realize? I have always heard yeah, being fat is bad that has been there quietly, but it never was too specific. It all seemed about looks, everyone is always talking about looks. But what about my freaking health?! 

The only one's who ever were brave enough to bring up my health were my parents but they were too scared of making me feel bad and they didn't approach it well, but I can't blame them. How do you talk about such a thing? I think changing how we form the conversation maybe? Not sure, I can only know what would have maybe helped me because telling me I might end up in a wheelchair did not help me. I knew I wouldn't because I love exercise too much. I loved food more and that is how I got fat. But with movement I am stubborn, I will exercise no matter what. As a teen I had a cast on and still figure skated even though that was how I broke it in the first place. I just knew I would never allow myself to end up in a wheelchair.And I guess that is how I got to where I am working on this. But nobody tells people how insidious and gradual the health problems can creep up. 

I hear of heart disease and diabetes but when you are feeling kind of ok you don't think that can ever happen to you! Nobody tells you that you can feel completely FINE leading up to a major health problem like a heart attack. Nobody tells you that all those things that seem just kind of annoying right now, like that slight knee pain or stomachache after eating could later turn into something that is debilitating and then you will have an even harder time over coming it.

Nobody I have talked to in my life about this seems to think that way. Like oh sure, for years my weight didn't make me feel that bad, losing it was only about looks and that was just not a good enough reason for me apparently. But now I have been really sick on and off for years and it is a huge war I am waging against my ill health. It is not easy, and I don't even have it as bad as some people do.So yeah I'm angry, I'm ticked that frequent indigestion and other unpleasant bathroom issues are not shouted about that they are a sign of worse to come! That you better get your butt in gear and do something now or you may end up in the hospital having your gallbladder removed. So far I have avoided that thank God. But here I am sick today, AGAIN, not as sick as usual. But oh the pain I could have avoided if I had known how bad it can get. I have gone through so many horrible gallbladder attacks working on my weight loss. Nobody tells you, until it happens, that losing weight can trigger this crap.

I just am so frustrated with the body positive movement, I get it. I don't want my thin, but not supermodel thin, 12 year old to feel ugly, and she shouldn't. But I do want the obese 12 year olds, and every overweight person, out there to know they doesn't deserve to be fat, that they are worthy and deserve health and vitality and that losing weight is the way to get it.

What we eat matters, how much of it we eat matters, exercise matters. These are not simply things we do for vanity sake, this is about living life and enjoying it instead of getting tired after every meal. Instead of having constant sugar cravings, instead of waking up thinking about food....waking up thinking about doing something that excites you. It's about being productive and feeling great about yourself. This is about not ending up in the hospital when you are older and your kids are crying and sad because their parent is sick and they are afraid of losing them. This is about not being a huge and expensive burden to our children when we are old. This is about not spending another day sick all because I wanted to eat king size snickers bars every day and actually thought that was ok! It is about that not being the highlight of my day!

I have only lost 20 pounds but my life is already better, so much better. Sugar, booze, chips, pizza, none of it is worth losing my life for. And I am not only speaking of death, I am speaking of whether or not I am living my life or stuck sick in the bathroom or in a bed because of my weight making me sick. Or whether I am actually living or just sitting in front of a TV shoving more food in my mouth like an addict who can't get enough.

I too think she was just having a sweet moment with Tyrion and didn't realize what she had said as being wrong. But then she did realize it I'm sure. Maybe now her and Dany will get along better. Sansa just seems really loyal to Jon and her family above all.
Oh goodness most women I know are anti-feminist....

I actually have never thought really fat people were lazy. I throughout my entire life, including the thin years, have known some super hard working fat people including my own mother. She used to be fat. But she hated sitting still, she just ate too much. I never really saw her sitting still. She was constantly working all day every day and she enjoyed walks too.She was on a depression medication that made her hungry and well, she was still depressed so she ate too much. She has no problem saying she ate too much. But she certainly wasn't a lazy person. She got off that med that wasn't working and stopped eating too much and she got thin.I have never thought that fat people are lazy because you can actually be pretty active and not lose weight, it has to do with food intake mostly. I will even say stress is a factor as well. But stress often can be an underlying reason people...tada...overeat.So it's too much food. Yeah stress and all makes it harder to lose weight, not impossible though.Anyway. Most fat people I know do actually work pretty hard in other areas of their lives. And many of them do stay on their feet all day, just they eat too much. They snack, they have too big of a supper, they stay up too late and eat too much late at night and go over their calories.Really irks me that anyone would think I hate fat people or think they are lazy just because I believe they can and should lose weight. Yeah some of them maybe are lazy, but I never assume things about people's personality based on their size. I will assume they are eating too much though if they are fat. But that isn't a personality or moral thing, I would say some don't realize just how much they are eating. I know I didn't. Self-awareness and education about why we are fat are important.
Yeah, just not eating meat doesn't automatically mean you are not eating too many calories for you body. For sure.

Are the only people who are allowed to be body positive or fat advocates those that have been obese since birth? Oh wait.....who the heck is obese from birth?!   
Nobody.   
Where are all these "naturally fat" people? Nobody is naturally fat. Certainly nobody is naturally obese. That just doesn't make any sense. You cannot tell me that you just turned fat for no reason.   
You can't say that despite only eating 1500 calories a day you ended up obese. That just doesn't happen.   
People who over eat get fat, people who don't over eat don't get fat. Fat people who eat less and move more lose weight and they keep it off if they keep eating the proper amount.   
I think the idea that diets fail and people gain the weight back comes from the fact if you diet then go back to eating too much food you do gain the weight back. Yes, that is true.   
There is no diet that will make you lose weight then allow you to go back to eating unrestricted and not get fat again. You have to eat the proper amount of calories for LIFE.

[https://www.health.harvard.edu/staying-healthy/the-truth-about-metabolism](https://www.health.harvard.edu/staying-healthy/the-truth-about-metabolism)   


I really don't think it has that big of an effect on weight loss or gain. Not to say it has none, but if you aren't seeing results, adjust what you are doing.

I wish I could make myself stay off sugar forever cuz when I dont eat bread or sugar I feel superhuman! The energy and sleep is like nothing I ever experienced before. But for now I can only seem to stick with moderation.

items.text:
Things Ross did that were really awesome.
Bought Phoebe that bike then helped her learn to ride.   


Of course the whole was going to take Rachel to her prom thing.   


When Joey was mad at Chandler over the Kathy thing and Joey said Ross was in the running to be his new best friend, first thing he did as his new best friend was get him to talk to Chandler.   


Went to a lot of trouble to try and get Rachel into that new apartment in his building. 

&#x200B;

When Rachel and he go to the sonogram he is really sweet with her and helps her find the baby on the monitor and he is pretty patient with her during the whole pregnancy. Very helpful and kind to her. He even stops dating toward the end of her pregnancy to be at her beck and call 24/7 as she asked. He is overall a really good dad. 

&#x200B;

Can ya'll think of anymore? Was just thinking about all the Ross is so annoying posts and these came to my mind as moments where I really loved his character.

Yes this. And if she is overweight herself? A criticism of her own weight. It is not your fault. Many people react this way. 
But she can't force you to the doctor for a  eating disorder. You are 18. But if you wanted to go so that you could get the doctors blessing then maybe that would get her to back off about it.
That is surprising. I must be looking at different plans. When I see anti-inflammatory advice it nixes all grains usually.

Thought of another, when he saw Carol get left alone at that restaurant by Susan who had to run to work or something. He asks her to come sit with him and his date. Course he was rude to his date. But the caring of how Carol must have felt was sweet.

My legs get smaller, my fingers get smaller, my face is less puffy looking, all the swollen lymph nodes I get in my arm pit area shrink down to normal. It is like I get thinner all over right away.   
And all the issues that I know can be made worse by inflammation go away. My sinuses clear up, my skin clears, my vision is clearer, my energy goes WAY up it is insane. My sleep is like perfect, I can fall asleep fast and wake with energy.   
Really everything gets better. My reaction time is faster, my performance in dance class is so much better.
Wow, and to protect the fat person jumping too. Imagine the injury if the trampoline broke. Yikes. Or simply if when you jump you hit the ground from stretching the trampoline.

I have had to practice intuitive eating. Meaning, I have had to learn to eat when I am only actually physically hungry instead of eating when I am trying to stuff emotions. It took me years of practice. YEARS. But I had to deprive myself to begin to learn to do this. It was by feeling deprived I realized I wasn't really depriving myself of anything good at all. And I still struggle at times.
I would honestly skip the drinks, I would always eat more when I drank. So water with lemon or something. Or a diet soda. Then I could enjoy my food more.

Yeah we got a lot of "you can't lock them in their room for life" comments when we began. But now they see what our kids do all the time and realize they are far from locked away from the world. Just ignore and eventually they will come around, or not, either way this is your life and your kid and they can buzz off. When family is that pushy about my life choices I literally just have to tell them to leave me alone about this choice, they got to say their piece already, nagging you won't make you change your mind. And it is ok to tell them that.

Thing is if you lose weight other things get better too. It isn't a cure all for life but it helps a lot. Just like money isn't a cure all but it helps to have enough to live.

Last time I lost a lot of weight my chiropractor told me I was looking very svelte.  I have to say, that feels good. I want to lose weight. I will respect myself more if I lose weight. I respect myself now. But I enjoy doing things I can be proud of. And that's ok. And it ticks me off these anti weight loss nutjobs think there is something wrong with that. The lack of respect they claim to get for being fat is exactly what they are doing to thin fit people. They are hypocrites.
I want to look better. I do not look half as attractive fat. Obesity is not pretty. This should be ok to say. I like my hair. I like my legs. I like my face. But I do not like my excess fat because it is too much. It is hurting me. I need to get rid of it. Period.

Haha, Sharney ads. I love Sharney and Julius. They are inspiring and don't charge a fortune and a half for their program like some do. It was too strict for me long term but I do like their inspiration and fb group so I kept it.

Some of that old fat logic is still stuck in my brain. And some of the bad diet advice. Like if I'm not dropping tons of weight fast it must not be working. Also annoyed when other people try to take credit for what I am doing now. "Oh I told you to do that awhile back." Really? First no you didn't and second why even say that??? SMH

Nobody has ever suggested actual calorie counting or how many to eat etc.

I am proud of what I have accomplished and I am taking credit for all of it. I have let others hold me back with their opinions for too long. I am doing this my way, for me. Period. 
And for my kids cuz I dont want them to think obese is normal. And dont want them to be embarrassed by me.

Thank you for the encouragement!
